summary: xargs turns lines of input into arguments for another command. Use it when a command like rm, touch, or wc takes file names as arguments but you have the names as output from find, ls, or grep.
notes: wc -l does not read file names from a pipe. find cs -name "*.py" | xargs wc -l runs wc -l with both names, so it counts lines in each file and prints a total.
With -I {}, xargs runs the command once per line: cp quiz1.txt quiz1.txt.bak, then quiz2, then quiz3.
find has its own safe version: find . -name "*.bak" -print0 | xargs -0 rm handles any file name, even ones with spaces or new lines.
pitfall: File names with spaces split into two arguments. ls lab*.txt | xargs rm tries to remove lab and report.txt and fails with rm: cannot remove 'lab': No such file or directory.
